role: (a) known reference in the WWOX context: preparation and readout control
intervention_and_identity: d-AP5 (GtoPdb 4168), 50 uM as used by Breton 2021; competitive NMDAR antagonist, tool compound
c1_generating_WWOX_observation: neuron-deleted slices burst (36/42) and bursts vanish with d-AP5 (51 bursts, 5 slices, 3 animals)
c2_inferred_step: that bursting requires NMDAR activity (observed); that NMDAR current is raised is NOT observed
c3_action_it_should_produce: complete NMDAR block: ceiling of the burst readout
c4_system: Synapsin-Cre Wwox KO neocortical L2/3 slices P13-P17, mouse
c6_result_that_would_weaken: if bursts survive d-AP5 in the new cohort the preparation differs from the source; if WT matched-trigger slices lose bursts equally, d-AP5 is generic
c7_measurement_distinguishing_from_alter: none (it cannot discriminate gain from permissive necessity); used as positive control and ceiling
ex_vivo_probe_utility: high as a readout control; zero as a mechanism test
next_experiment_priority: run in every slice as last step
systemic_plausibility: none (tool compound, no human exposure sought)
exposure_selectivity_safety_information: potency in WWOX preparation not stated in any catalogue row read; surmountable block
what_LEGEND_adds: a control role, stated as such

role: (a) known reference in the WWOX context: clinical anecdote, same function, different mechanism
intervention_and_identity: vigabatrin (ChEMBL CHEMBL89598, racemate, max phase 4); irreversible GABA-T inactivator
c1_generating_WWOX_observation: human WWOX-DEE case reports of spasm cessation/partial response (2 benefit, 3 null, 1 partial, 1 unresolved; queried, not full read, U20)
c2_inferred_step: raising ambient GABA offsets an inhibitory deficit (unmeasured in humans)
c3_action_it_should_produce: raises tissue GABA; acts on tonic and spillover pools more than on the amplitude of a quantal IPSC (prior knowledge, UNVERIFIED)
c4_system: human infants (anecdote); no WWOX slice or mouse arm exists
c5a_acute_effect_on_endpoint: not testable in acute slice (inactivation is slow); a chronic mouse arm would be needed
c5b_functional_benefit_during_exposure: possible (clinical reports are of spasms, a different seizure type from slice bursts)
c5c_compensation_of_impaired_function: a compensation of lost inhibition only if tonic GABA is the limiting term; not shown
c6_result_that_would_weaken: if tonic GABA conductance is unchanged in KO slices and an NNC-711 or tiagabine arm does not move bursts, the ambient-GABA reading of K2 is weakened
c7_measurement_distinguishing_from_alter: tonic current (gabazine- or picrotoxin-sensitive holding current) and phasic IPSC charge in the same cells, KO v HT v WT
suppression_toxicity_controls: VABAM and visual field safety limits (boxed warning, US label 2026-06-15); in WWOX records, MRI abnormality in two cases (A-VGB-7)
ex_vivo_probe_utility: poor for acute slice; usable only after chronic exposure in mouse
next_experiment_priority: low priority for slice work; belongs to H02 exposure-limit card
systemic_plausibility: human use exists (label: infantile spasms, refractory partial seizures, 2 years and over)
exposure_selectivity_safety_information: US label and ChEMBL give identity and class; potency at brain GABA-T not stated; Ki 850 uM is a time-dependent inactivation constant
what_LEGEND_adds: the question it answers (phasic charge v ambient GABA) is new; the compound is not
state: KNOWN; not a test of the sIPSC deficit

intervention_and_identity: clobazam (CHEMBL70418) and its metabolite N-desmethylclobazam (CHEMBL2260842), benzodiazepine-site PAM at gamma2-containing GABA-A receptors; probes to attribute subunit: zolpidem v clonazepam
c1_generating_WWOX_observation: sIPSC amplitude 57.3 to 27.5 pA (about -52 percent; pooled controls and pooled events; KS tests WT v KO and HT v KO both significant; HT v WT not reported); largest stated KO effect but not the only KO-v-HT difference (mEPSC and sEPSC amplitude also differ); Pvalb mRNA lower 4 of 4 contrasts, Gabrg2 transcript present (about 32 to 53 TPM) and not lowered beyond control-line variation (P3a deposits)
c2_inferred_step: that the lost current is receptor-limited at gamma2 synapses (UNMEASURED: it could be release-limited; Gabra1 mRNA is lower in H_S (log2 -1.21, beyond the -0.41 control-line difference) and within that band in the other contrasts)
c3_action_it_should_produce: increase fast GABA-A charge in the presence of released GABA (GABA-dependent, no direct gating); at EC10 GABA 1.3 to 2.5 fold and mostly longer decay (Ralvenius), so restoration of a roughly halved amplitude to control is not guaranteed
c4_system: KO and HT and WT neocortical L2/3 slices, same preparation as Breton 2021, mouse; human exposure species-mix (parent plus metabolite) not reproducible in slice
c5a_acute_effect_on_endpoint: hypothesised: lower burst frequency with IPSC charge restored
c5b_functional_benefit_during_exposure: hypothesised: during exposure only, burst control without loss of evoked responses
c5c_compensation_of_impaired_function: hypothesised class: compensation of the impaired inhibitory function (a hypothesis, not a finding; repair v counterbalance not separated by E2)
c6_result_that_would_weaken: IPSC charge restored but bursts continue; burst reduction equal in WT matched-trigger slices (network state, not KO specificity); charge not restorable (then the arm is uninterpretable); E0 showing a release-limited locus or an excitatory-gain/Ih difference sufficient alone
c7_measurement_distinguishing_from_alter: IPSC charge, NMDAR current and Vm in the same KO cells; WT with gabazine-matched IPSC deficit; zolpidem v clonazepam to attribute alpha1 v alpha2/3
suppression_toxicity_controls: F-I curve and Rin unchanged; evoked fEPSP slope in WT unchanged; viability; washout; same agent in WT matched-trigger slices (suppression index)
ex_vivo_probe_utility: good as a probe of the inhibitory limiting-step; the in vivo species mix needs both parent and metabolite
next_experiment_priority: first among the drug arms after the same-cell triad
systemic_plausibility: plausible only as an idea: clinical benzodiazepines are tried in WWOX-DEE (WOREE refractory); no WWOX-specific result found; tolerance, sedation and respiratory warnings from label
exposure_selectivity_safety_information: identity (ChEMBL) and class mechanism; label: LGS adjunct 2 years and over, boxed warnings; subtype data exist in three primary papers, selectivity disputed (EC50 about 0.1 to 1 uM; see ladder L05, L06)
what_LEGEND_adds: a context for a known drug class: sufficiency and correction in the same preparation with HT and Cre+ WT controls, charge not amplitude, metabolite included; not a new name
state: HYPOTHESIS; subtype data exist, selectivity disputed; conditional on E0 (receptor-limited locus) and on the selectivity dispute

role: (c) alternative acting on the same function by a different mechanism
intervention_and_identity: tiagabine (CHEMBL1027; HCl CHEMBL1695), GAT1 inhibitor; tool NNC-711
c1_generating_WWOX_observation: same sIPSC deficit; K2 anecdote as a GABA-raising reference
c2_inferred_step: that released GABA is cleared too fast or too little is released: prolongs IPSC and raises tonic current (prior knowledge, UNVERIFIED)
c3_action_it_should_produce: GAT1 inhibition: IC50 70 nM hGAT1 versus 1.41 mM rat GAT2, 917 uM human GAT3, 1.67 mM hBGT-1 (ChEMBL, mixed species)
c5a_acute_effect_on_endpoint: hypothesised: lower bursts if release is preserved and clearance limits
c6_result_that_would_weaken: no effect on bursts although IPSC decay is prolonged (extra GABA at receptors does not stop bursts), or paradoxical increase (tonic excitation of interneurons or spillover)
c7_measurement_distinguishing_from_alter: IPSC decay and tonic holding current vs burst frequency; compare with H1 at matched IPSC charge
suppression_toxicity_controls: same as H1; plus excitability of interneurons
ex_vivo_probe_utility: good probe separating release/clearance from receptor limitation
next_experiment_priority: second drug arm, same slices as H1
systemic_plausibility: label limits: adults and children 12 and over, partial seizures; no WWOX result
exposure_selectivity_safety_information: ChEMBL and GtoPdb human GAT1 potency; selectivity values mix species; label 2021 (US)
what_LEGEND_adds: tests whether the lost inhibition is receptor-limited (H1) or release-limited (A1)

role: (d) counter-hypothesis able to refute the interpretation
intervention_and_identity: ezogabine = retigabine (CHEMBL41355), Kv7 opener; reversal with XE991; selective-tool ICA-069673
c1_generating_WWOX_observation: resting potential graded -79.25/-75.51/-73.62 mV (HT and KO v WT, cells as independent units; HT v KO not tested, gap 1.9 mV); Rin 143.26 v 143.03 MOhm shared; rebound significant only in KO
c2_inferred_step: that a Kv7 (M-current) deficit sets the depolarised state (UNMEASURED: Kcnq2 mRNA inside control-line band; Kcnq3 -1.07 in H_S only)
c3_action_it_should_produce: shift Kv7 gating to hyperpolarised voltages; hyperpolarises any neuron with Kv7
c5a_acute_effect_on_endpoint: hypothesised (counter): bursts stop at a Vm-restoring concentration
c6_result_that_would_weaken: if Kv7 opening to the control Vm leaves KO bursts intact and a Vm-matched WT/HT slice does not burst, intrinsic depolarisation is not sufficient and H1 gains; if the opener stops bursts and Vm-matched WT slices burst, H1 is weakened
c7_measurement_distinguishing_from_alter: XE991-sensitive current in KO v HT v WT cells; opener titrated to the Vm shift of 5.6 mV; Vm-matched (bath K+) WT slices
suppression_toxicity_controls: same opener in WT matched-trigger slices (suppression index); firing-reduction counts only with viability and recovery
ex_vivo_probe_utility: good as a refuter; also a probe of the XE991 pair
next_experiment_priority: third drug arm; rewritten from P3a C2 (its depolarisation premise is shared with HT)
systemic_plausibility: ezogabine: serious adverse-event history (not verified here); azetukalner phase 3; no WWOX result
exposure_selectivity_safety_information: EC50 spread up to about 9-fold across assays and isoforms (0.43 to 4.38 uM KCNQ2/3 in ChEMBL; oocyte Kv7.2 2.6, Kv7.5 15, Kv7.4 22, Kv7.2/7.3 2.4 uM, verifier-reported); azetukalner 98 nM one assay not transferred; withdrawal history secondary-level; no openFDA label
what_LEGEND_adds: demotes P3a C2 to a refuter using the heterozygote as the control P3a did not use

role: (d2) non-pharmacological necessity and sufficiency tools (not candidates)
intervention_and_identity: gabazine titration (CHEMBL32503; GtoPdb 4197) and bath K+; TTX 1 uM as a generic silencer
c2_inferred_step: sufficiency of a single deficit in a normal circuit (gabazine) shows sufficiency, not that it is the KO step; bath K+ is not Vm-matching (no Rin, sag or rebound)
c3_action_it_should_produce: antagonise GABA-A at the GABA site (titrated); depolarise by K+; silence by Na+ channel block
c4_system: WT and HT slices, same preparation
c6_result_that_would_weaken: if neither single manipulation produces d-APV-sensitive bursts, no single deficit is sufficient (interaction or secondary state)
c7_measurement_distinguishing_from_alter: charge fraction measured in the same cells before burst scoring
suppression_toxicity_controls: TTX arm confirms bursts are activity-driven and that a firing-reduction readout is trivially satisfied by any silencer
exposure_selectivity_safety_information: gabazine: no affinity in the catalogue rows read; titration is empirical
what_LEGEND_adds: the sufficiency matrix is the new element
